content: 1. Mefloquine may increase the QTc-prolonging effects of high-risk QTc-prolonging agents. This interaction can lead to significant toxicity, including cardiac arrhythmias. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug when possible. If unavoidable, monitor the patient closely with ECGs. 2. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of quetiapine by prolonging the QTc interval. This combination should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. If co-administration is necessary, monitor the patient closely for signs of cardiac toxicity. 3. Mefloquine enhances the QTc-prolonging effects of quinidine, increasing the risk of ECG abnormalities and cardiac arrest. This combination is contraindicated. Use an alternative drug. 4. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of quinine by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, monitor the patient closely. 5. Mefloquine and quizartinib both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of cardiac toxicity. Modify therapy or monitor the patient closely with frequent ECGs if co-administered. 6. Mefloquine increases the levels or effects of repotrectinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 7. Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction also increases the risk of QTc prolongation. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, monitor the patient closely. 8. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 9. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 10. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 11. Mefloquine increases the levels of rifaximin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 12. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of mefloquine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Avoid co-administration with drugs that have a known risk of Torsade de Pointes. 13. Mefloquine increases the levels or effects of rimegepant by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 14. Mefloquine increases the levels or effects of riociguat by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Monitor for signs of hypotension and adjust the dose if necessary. 15. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of risperidone by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 16. Ritonavir increases the levels of mefloquine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism, leading to increased toxicity. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, monitor the patient closely for signs of toxicity. 17. Mefloquine decreases the levels of ritonavir by an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, but monitor the patient closely. 18. Mefloquine increases the levels of rivaroxaban by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely, especially in patients with renal impairment, as this may increase bleeding risk. 19. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated and monitor the patient closely. 20. Mefloquine increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, but monitor the patient closely. 21. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of salmeterol by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 22. Selpercatinib increases the toxicity of mefloquine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 23. Sertraline increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Mefloquine also increases the toxicity of sertraline by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 24. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of sevoflurane by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 25. Mefloquine increases the levels of silodosin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 26. Siponimod and mefloquine both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of cardiac toxicity. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 27. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of solifenacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 28. Sorafenib and mefloquine both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of cardiac toxicity. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 29. Mefloquine increases the levels of sotalol by decreasing its metabolism. This combination also increases the risk of QTc prolongation. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 30. Stiripentol affects hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism as both an inhibitor and inducer. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates co-administered with stiripentol for increased or decreased effects, and adjust dosages as needed. 31. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of sulfamethoxazole by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 32. Sunitinib and mefloquine both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of cardiac toxicity. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 33. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of tacrolimus by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 34. Mefloquine increases the levels or effects of talazoparib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 35. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of tamoxifen by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 36. Mefloquine increases the levels or effects of tazemetostat by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 37. Tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 38. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of tetrabenazine by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 39. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 40. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of thioridazine by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 41. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of thiothixene by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 42. Ticagrelor increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 43. Mefloquine increases the levels of timolol by decreasing its metabolism, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 44. Mefloquine increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 45. Tipranavir increases the levels of mefloquine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism, leading to increased toxicity. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 46. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of tizanidine by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 47. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of tolterodine by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 48. Mefloquine increases the levels of topotecan by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 49. Mefloquine and toremifene both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of cardiac toxicity. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, closely monitor the patient with ECGs. 50. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of trimethoprim by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 51. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of trimipramine by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 52. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the dose of CYP3A4 substrates according to product labeling. 53. Mefloquine decreases the effects of the live typhoid vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. 54. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Exercise extreme caution when co-administering vilanterol with drugs that prolong the QTc interval. 55. Valbenazine and mefloquine both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of cardiac toxicity. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 56. Mefloquine decreases the levels of valproic acid by an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, but monitor the patient closely. 57. Mefloquine and vandetanib both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of cardiac toxicity. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, monitor the patient closely with ECGs. 58. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of vardenafil by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 59. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of vemurafenib by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Mefloquine may also increase vemurafenib levels. 60. Mefloquine increases the levels or effects of venetoclax by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 50% and monitor for signs of toxicity. 61. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of venlafaxine by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 62. Mefloquine increases the levels of verapamil by decreasing its metabolism. Verapamil also increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 63. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Exercise extreme caution when co-administering vilanterol with drugs that prolong the QTc interval. 64. Mefloquine increases the levels of vincristine liposomal by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 65. Voclosporin and mefloquine both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of cardiac toxicity. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 66. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism, leading to increased toxicity. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 67. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of vorinostat by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 68. Mefloquine increases the effects of warfarin by an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 69. Zileuton increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely.
